title: Glucose syrup: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: Glucose syrup is a thick, sweet liquid made by breaking down starch (usually corn or wheat) into simple sugars. It sweetens products and helps control texture, moisture and crystallisation.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use glucose syrup as a sweetener/sugar and it is of plant origin.
Our rules read glucose syrup as a refined syrup.

Our scorer looks for glucose syrup when Autoimmune Protocol (AIP), Diabetes, Gout or Fatty liver (NAFLD) is on for you. If those plans are off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
Labels do not all use the same word for this. Below is every spelling we watch for. Some come from other languages, because a pack made for another country prints its own.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
